children: Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK.B) is moving into a new phase of its leadership transition, with Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio) leaving the chairman role and becoming chairman emeritus, effective immediately.

The board elected Howard G. Buffett, Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio)'s son and a director since 1993, as chairman. Greg Abel has been Berkshire's chief executive since the start of 2026 after Buffett stepped aside from that position.
Berkshire said Buffett will remain on the board and continue offering his perspective. Chairman emeritus is an honorary role that allows a former chairman to stay connected to the company.

The company also kept Susan Decker as lead independent director. Howard Buffett has led the Howard G. Buffett Foundation since 1999 and is expected to focus on preserving Berkshire's culture rather than overseeing daily operations.

He has also held board positions at companies including Coca-Cola, ConAgra Foods and Archer-Daniels-Midland. Berkshire remains one of the largest U.S. companies, with a market value around $1.1 trillion. The transition follows Buffett's decades-long leadership, while Berkshire said its culture and values will remain central under the new structure.
Shares of Berkshire dipped 1% after the news on Friday.

title: Berkshire Hathaway stock drops as Warren Buffett exits chairman role
